subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation - GPU sizing & SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity sizing & SLOs (Acme)

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and a set of follow-ups to help Rafael and our infra team validate sizing for a Redwood Dedicated deployment: 

1) SLO targets (please confirm):
   - p50 / p95 generation latency: p95 target = 250ms for single-turn streaming responses (end-to-end, token surface).
   - Throughput target: sustained 400 requests/sec (RPS) with spikes to 900 RPS for 5–10 minute bursts.
   - Concurrency: up to 1,000 concurrent open streaming sessions during peak.
   - Burst concurrency: up to 1,500 for <30 minutes.

2) Model & workload details (please attach traffic profile if available):
   - Model family: customer will serve a 32k-context foundation model (customer-provided variant).
   - Average input length: ~120 tokens; average generated tokens per request: ~350 tokens.
   - Streaming requirements: first-byte latency critical; we should target sub-100ms token latency where possible for the initial tokens.

3) Validation plan asks (what Rafael needs to size infra):
   - Representative traffic CSV (timestamped RPS/concurrency) and 5–10 representative requests (prompts).
   - Any hard QPS/RPS limits from upstream throttles or client-side constraints.
   - Budget guidance / preferred GPU types (H100 vs A100 vs L4) and any procurement constraints.

Next steps we propose: Rafael will run a short benchmark on our side using your traffic profile and report back on: expected reserved throughput (tokens/sec), recommended GPU mix, and an initial plan for a 72-hour validation window on Dedicated.

Can you share the traffic CSV and confirm the SLO numbers above? If anything on our recap is off, call it out and I’ll correct.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
[Attachment: proposal_dedicated_capacity_v1.pdf]

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-team@acme.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity sizing & SLOs (Acme)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming and adding details below; attaching our traffic profile CSV and a short sample of typical prompts.

Confirmed SLOs/Workload:
- p95 target: 250ms for token emit for streaming clients (we understand the challenge; this is our customer-facing goal).
- Sustained throughput: 420 RPS average; typical daytime 600 RPS; night baseline ~80 RPS.
- Peak bursts: up to 1,200 RPS for short campaigns (5–15 minutes).
- Concurrency: normally ~750 open streams; peaks to 1,100 concurrently.
- Model: we’ll be running a 32k-context LLM (internal fork of an open family). Average prompt size ~100–140 tokens, avg generated tokens ~320.

Budget / GPU preference:
- We prefer H100 for latency-critical traffic. Budget is constrained though — if A100 provides acceptable p95 for our traffic, we may choose A100 for cost parity. L4 is not an option for this model class.

Files attached: acme_traffic_profile.csv, sample_prompts.txt

Let us know when Rafael can start the benchmark and what you need for a short validation window (IPs, whitelist, temporary credentials).

Best,
Jane Doe
Director, Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
[jane.doe@acme.com]
[Attachments: acme_traffic_profile.csv, sample_prompts.txt]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:40:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity sizing & SLOs (Acme)

Marissa / Aditya —

Thanks Jane for the traffic profile — that helps a lot. Quick internal notes + proposed validation/test plan for Acme: 

Summary of initial sizing assumptions (rough):
- Target model similar to 70B-parameter 32k-context; expected tokens/sec per H100 ~ 110–130 tokens/sec sustained (depends on quantization).
- For A100, expect ~70–90 tokens/sec sustained under similar quantization.
- Based on your average 320 tokens per request and 600 RPS daytime spike, token throughput target = 600 * 320 = ~192k tokens/sec during spikes.

Preliminary recommended reserved capacity (initial):
- H100 pool: 4–6 GPUs reserved for latency-critical tier (can serve ~440–780 RPS depending on batching and KV cache effectiveness).
- A100 pool: 8–10 GPUs for cost-optimized baseline capacity.
- Autoscale policy: reserve baseline on A100, overflow to H100 for latency-sensitive routes during spikes.

Proposed 72-hour validation window plan: 
- Day 0: Mirror traffic (read-only) to Dedicated test routing for 3 hours to validate request shapes and token emit characteristics.
- Day 1: Controlled ramp up to 70% of expected peak RPS using sample_prompts, measure p50/p95 and token latency.
- Day 2: Full peak soak test with burst profile (simulate 1,200 RPS bursts), evaluate tail latency, OOMs, and sustained throughput.

What we need from Acme to start the run:
- Whitelist IPs or temporary VPN access info (we can provide an allowlist).
- A short list of 10–15 canonical prompts (you attached sample_prompts.txt — that's perfect).
- Confirmation of whether we should test with H100-only, A100-only, or both in a split run.

I’ll attach the benchmark result template after the first dry run. I also ran a quick micro-benchmark on a dev H100 rig and attached the raw CSV (gpu_benchmark_results.csv) — this is noisy but shows H100 ~120 tokens/sec on the short sample (128-token generation).

Jane — if that plan looks good, can you confirm whitelist details and whether we should run both GPU types? I’ll schedule the tests for next week (Mon–Wed window) pending your signoff.

Thanks —
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
[Attachments: gpu_benchmark_results.csv, validation_plan.md]
